# About this book {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| include: false
source("_setup.R")
```

This book reports one analysis. Replace this paragraph with one sentence on what the analysis decides, for whom, and on what data.

<!-- Q
- What decision does this book support?
- Who will read it, and what do they already know?
-->

## What is in it, and in what order {.unnumbered}

The order of the parts is an argument.

1. **The data and the instrument.** What was measured, and how well.
2. **What this design could detect.** The detection floor.
3. **Results.**
4. **Robustness.** Whether the results survive small changes to the analysis.
5. **Synthesis.** The only chapter that interprets.
6. **Reference.** Methods, provenance, limitations, and glossary.

The detection floor comes before any result. A result read without its detection floor is a result read without its denominator.

## The register rule {#sec-register .unnumbered}

Every chapter before the synthesis is descriptive and quantitative. It says what was measured, and how large it was.

::: {.content-hidden when-profile="gallery"}
Interpretation lives only in @sec-interpretation, under a banner that says it is a reading, not a result.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="gallery"}
Interpretation lives only in the synthesis chapter, under a banner that says it is a reading, not a result. In this gallery, that chapter is @sec-g-interpretation.
:::

The rule is enforced by `tools/style/register_guard.py`. Run every check with `bash scripts/check_style.sh`.

## The questions each section must answer {.unnumbered}

Each section carries the questions its prose must answer, as an HTML comment that starts with `<!-- Q`. The comments are hidden in a normal render. Render with `quarto render --profile draft` to show each block as a collapsed callout.

## Colour and accessibility {.unnumbered}

- One palette serves the whole book. It is safe for the common forms of colour-vision deficiency.
- Categories use the Okabe-Ito colours [@okabeito].
- Significance is encoded by shape as well as colour. No reader depends on colour alone.
- A heatmap of row z-scores shows each feature relative to its own mean. A z-score is not absolute expression.

## Reproducing it {.unnumbered}

```bash
quarto render                   # this book
quarto render --profile draft   # this book, with the draft questions shown
bash scripts/check_style.sh     # every style check and test
```
